## Download the data

- [cassava_mosaic_survey.xlsx](data/cassava_mosaic_survey.xlsx): cassava mosaic disease survey, Nigeria, 2015 and 2017
- [bean_week6.csv](data/bean_week6.csv): week-6 measurements from a common bean trial, Bells University of Technology

## Cassava mosaic disease survey

Eni, A., Efekemo, O., Onile-ere, O. and Pita, J. (2021). *Survey of cassava mosaic begomoviruses across South-west and North central regions of Nigeria in 2015 and 2017.* Mendeley Data, V1. [doi:10.17632/mpj2nxk3tk.1](https://doi.org/10.17632/mpj2nxk3tk.1)

The accompanying paper is Eni et al. (2021), *Annals of Applied Biology*, [doi:10.1111/aab.12647](https://doi.org/10.1111/aab.12647).

The data are shared under a [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) licence and are used here unmodified. Thank you to the WAVE team at Covenant University for making them openly available.

## Common bean trial

From Raphael Odera Onunkwor's final-year thesis at Bells University of Technology. The full reanalysis, raw data and code are at [github.com/Onunkwor/pvfta1-phenology](https://github.com/Onunkwor/pvfta1-phenology) (MIT licence).

## Software and further reading

- [R for Plant Disease Epidemiology](https://r4pde.net) by Emerson M. Del Ponte: an open textbook, and the best next step after this workshop.
- [epifitter](https://cran.r-project.org/package=epifitter) by Kaique Alves and Emerson Del Ponte, for fitting disease progress curves. Lesson 2 uses its powdery mildew data.
- R, RStudio, and the `readxl`, `dplyr`, `ggplot2` and `lme4` packages.
